correctness.rationale: The 2x2 transient generator gives the backward equations and exactly \(M=N/(2e^2+zN)\). Its smallest negative eigenvalue gives \(\Lambda=z+(c+3e-\Delta)/2\). Both derivatives are algebraically reconstructed and checked. With \(b>a\), \(H_M\) decreases strictly to a negative value and \(H_T\) increases strictly to +infinity, yielding unique maxima/minima. The strict global comparison \(\ell/\Delta>2e^2/(N^2-2e^2)\) is proved by a positive factorization, establishing \(z_M<z_T\) and \(d_T\le d_M\). Boundary equality yields uniqueness at zero. Replayed symbolic/rational/numeric checker passed 2518 assertions; the infinite-parameter conclusion rests on the proof rather than finite testing.

originality.rationale: The inspected full preprint by Wagner–Ross–Possingham derives a different discrete-time catastrophe/colonization matrix and optimizes a quasi-stationary eigenvalue, not the strict ordering of its optimizer against the fully occupied initial-state mean optimizer for the explicitly defined continuous-time common-shock chain. The mean-versus-tail distinctions in McCarthy–Thompson–Possingham, Blowes–Connolly and Grimm–Wissel concern other population formulations/objectives and do not imply the present three-regime classification from inspected accessible material. Exact background formulas and objective concepts are not claimed as novel. Residual risk from inaccessible full texts and uncatalogued equivalent results is disclosed; absence of a matching search result is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: McCarthy–Thompson–Possingham and Blowes–Connolly full journal texts were not available for page-by-page comparison; their accessible descriptions are not whole-document exclusions.
The continuous-time common-shock model is a new specialization, not a proof of uniqueness of the ecological phenomenon in all metapopulations.
A published theorem in different notation or an unindexed archive might already imply the result; no external originality adjudication was performed.

value.rationale: The same two-reserve system supports two standard, scientifically different persistence objectives. The theorem identifies a structural universal *ordering* of their optimal spacing, and a nonempty intermediate parameter regime in which one objective selects coincident reserves while the other demands positive separation. Exact amplitude thresholds and uniqueness rule out ambiguous local optima under faster catastrophe-decay conditions. These are natural conservation-model comparisons beyond a parameter substitution or one-off numerical gain; no empirical management effectiveness is claimed.
